candidate.pattern_followed: src/ssl/record/rec_layer_s3.rs (stage/p25/rec-layer, d2440bb64): never form a typed slice over caller-supplied writable output; write through a raw pointer and publish only what was written.

authority.source: OpenSSL 3.5.9 providers/implementations/ciphers/ciphercommon_gcm.c (getivgen :121-135, setivinv :139-148, gcm_tls_cipher :549-608). C signatures take unsigned char *out; the EVP/provider ABI promises writable storage, never initialised values.
authority.abi: No #[no_mangle], #[export_name], #[repr(C)], extern "C" signature, exported symbol or allocator-seam constant changed. Diff lines containing no_mangle/repr(C)/export_name/extern "C": 0. Diff lines touching the allocator seam: 0.
authority_behaviour: getivgen: setiv(ctx->iv, ivlen) first; normalise olen (0 or >ivlen means ivlen); memcpy(out, iv + ivlen - olen, olen); ctr64_inc(iv + ivlen - 8); iv_state = IV_STATE_COPIED; return 1. All preserved.

gcm_tls_cipher: refuse unless out == in and len >= explicit_iv(8) + tag(16); encrypt increments tls_enc_records (FIPS A.5); explicit IV generated at out[0..8] on encrypt or read from out[0..8] on decrypt; in/out advance by 8, len loses 24; tag = out + len on encrypt (write) and in + len on decrypt (read); on decrypt failure OPENSSL_cleanse(out, len). All preserved.
The authority operates entirely through raw unsigned char pointers; it never requires the caller's output slots to hold initialised bytes.

getivgen.buffer: (*p).data, the application's output buffer supplied through OSSL_PARAM_construct_octet_string in evp/cipher_ctx.rs EVP_CTRL_GCM_IV_GEN
getivgen.nature: output only; the caller declares data_size writable bytes, not initialised bytes
output only; the record's explicit-IV slot may be uninitialised on entry (the C authority writes it here)

gcm_tls_cipher.caller: gcm_cipher_internal (only caller; line 1244, when ctx->tls_aad_len != UNINITIALISED_SIZET)
gcm_tls_cipher.buffer: forwards out, in_, len from the provider cipher-update dispatch

gcm_tls_cipher.caller: ossl_gcm_cipher -> AES/ARIA/SM4 GCM _FUNCTIONS tables -> EVP cupdate (EVP_EncryptUpdate/EVP_DecryptUpdate)
gcm_tls_cipher.buffer: application pointers. EVP_EncryptUpdate passes out/in through unchanged (cipher_ctx.rs:3821-3834); outsize is inl for the streaming GCM mode. EVP_CTRL_AEAD_TLS1_AAD is the TLS-record convention, and the authority requires out == in.
gcm_tls_cipher.nature: in-place record; the plaintext/ciphertext region is initialised by the caller or by receipt, while the explicit-IV and tag slots are outputs on encryption

gcm_tls_cipher.caller: tests in this module (tls_seal/tls_open and the new gcm_out_* tests)

gcm_tls_cipher.note: reach gcm_cipher_internal but stream_final passes in_ = NULL and len = 0, so gcm_tls_cipher's in_.is_null() guard refuses before any record work

site_1_getivgen.verdict: UNSOUND BEFORE: core::slice::from_raw_parts_mut(out, olen) formed a &mut [u8] over caller-writable memory. Both callers treat the destination as output-only; neither the C authority nor the provider ABI requires initialised u8 values there. The olen bytes are only written (copied from ctx->iv), but reference validity requires the whole extent to be initialised.
site_1_getivgen.change: The destination stays a raw pointer. When olen != 0, core::ptr::copy_nonoverlapping(src.as_ptr(), out, olen) writes exactly the bytes the authority's memcpy writes. No reference is formed over out. The source is the checked sub-slice of ctx->iv (initialised).
site_1_getivgen.state_transitions_preserved: setiv(ctx->iv, ivlen) before the copy; olen normalisation unchanged; ctr64_inc on ctx->iv[ivlen-8..] unchanged; iv_state = IV_STATE_COPIED unchanged. The new contract additionally states out must not overlap ctx->iv (the authority's memcpy has the same requirement).
site_1_getivgen.evidence: getivgen has exactly two callers (enumerated above); both pass output-only storage. The authority is a raw memcpy. The conversion eliminates the extra validity requirement the C code never had.

site_2_gcm_tls_cipher.verdict: THE ALIASING IS SOUND, THE WHOLE-RECORD SLICE WAS NOT. (a) Same allocation: the function refuses unless out == in_ (cast_mut), so every accepted call is in place; the C authority has the identical guard. (b) Initialised region covers everything READ: on encrypt, the explicit-IV slot is written by getivgen before use, the plaintext (8..len-16) is caller-initialised, and the tag slot is written, never read; on decrypt, the whole record is the received record and is initialised, so the explicit IV, ciphertext and received tag are all initialised. (c) Overlapping mutable references: split_at_mut produced disjoint mutable sub-slices, so two live &mut references to the same bytes were never created. The defect is narrower and real: from_raw_parts_mut(out, len) required all len bytes to be valid initialised u8 values at construction time, while on the encrypting path the explicit-IV slot and the tag slot are output-only and the provider ABI does not require them initialised. This is not an analogy: it is a legitimate in-place caller (the authority's own TLS record usage) whose output slots are uninitialised.
site_2_gcm_tls_cipher.change: The record stays a raw writable region. getivgen/setivinv receive out directly. payload = out.add(8) and tag_slot = payload.add(payload_len), both bounded by the already-checked len >= 24. A single raw pointer (payload) is passed as both the input and the output of the hardware one-shot, and tag_slot is its tag pointer, exactly the authority's in += 8 / out += 8 / tag arithmetic. The authentication failure cleanse writes payload_len bytes at payload. No typed reference is formed over the record anywhere in the function.
site_2_gcm_tls_cipher.tag_and_cleanse: Unchanged: the one-shot still calls CRYPTO_gcm128_finish with the full ctx->taglen on decryption (the constant-time full-length comparison lives there), the tag pointer is the same address as the authority's, and OPENSSL_cleanse still covers exactly payload_len bytes on decryption failure before the error tail.
site_2_gcm_tls_cipher.evidence: Callers enumerated above; in-place is enforced by the function itself, not assumed. The new gcm_out_in_place_record_encrypts_and_decrypts_at_one_address test leaves the explicit-IV and tag slots as MaybeUninit, encrypts in place, and decrypts the result back to the plaintext.

unsafe_ops.before_after: cipher_gcm.rs total unsafe blocks 66 -> 70. Production 47 -> 47; #[cfg(test)] 19 -> 23. unsafe fn declarations 39 -> 39.
unsafe_ops.eliminated: 2 whole-extent typed-slice constructions over caller-writable memory (getivgen: from_raw_parts_mut(out, olen); gcm_tls_cipher: from_raw_parts_mut(out, len) plus the split_at_mut views that depended on it).
unsafe_ops.relocated: Production unsafe work is now 3 explicit raw operations, all inside the existing function-level unsafe blocks: core::ptr::copy_nonoverlapping in getivgen, and two ptr::add computations in gcm_tls_cipher. Each carries a SAFETY comment stating extent and initialisation. The hardware one-shot call keeps its existing raw-pointer contract.

discharged: getivgen never reads its caller's output before writing it, and publishes exactly olen bytes (ivlen when olen is 0).
gcm_tls_cipher forms no reference over the record; every byte it reads is initialised on both directions, while write-only output slots may be uninitialised.
The in-place precondition out == in_ is enforced by the function, not assumed.
The tag slot address, the payload extent, the cleanse extent and the IV state transitions are unchanged from the authority.
retained: The provider ABI hands raw writable pointers; the caller's obligation to initialise the plaintext (encrypt) or supply a received record (decrypt) is documented on getivgen and gcm_tls_cipher, and cannot be type-enforced at this ABI.
Non-overlap of out with ctx/ctx->buf and of getivgen's out with ctx->iv is a documented precondition, matching the C memcpy/one-shot requirements; no current caller violates it.

compatibility_delta: No behaviour change intended. The explicit-IV bytes written, the invocation-field increment, payload/tag offsets, plen, tls_enc_records accounting, iv_state = IV_STATE_FINISHED and tls_aad_len reset, authentication refusal and the decryption-failure cleanse are all unchanged. Tests: the 13 pre-existing GCM tests plus the 5 new ones pass.
